newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds, NatWest staff to vote on strike -union.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds, NatWest staff to vote on strike -union.

text.p: Staff at UK banks Lloyds TSB and NatWest are being asked to vote in favour of a half-day strike on Christmas Eve, BIFU, the banking, insurance and finance union, said on Monday.
The union said in a statement that more than 35,000 staff at the two banks would be balloted on "a half-day strike to force closure of the banks on the afternoon of Tuesday, December 24".
English banks have traditionally closed early on Christmas Eve but this year Lloyds TSB want to stay open until 1630 GMT and NatWest want to stay open until 1530 GMT, BIFU added.
BIFU said NatWest's decision to stay open breached an agreement it reached in October to close at lunchtime.
"Bank staff deserve a Christmas break like other workers," said Ed Sweeney, general secretary of the union "They want time to join their families and enjoy Christmas," he added.
"Many banks plan to close at lunchtime and there's no evidence of any customer demand to pop into a bank on Christmas Eve afternoon."
More than 16,000 BIFU members in Scottish banks are being balloted in a separate dispute to defend their traditional January 2 bank holiday.
